63: // diff compares two multi-line strings and returns a helpful comment
64: func diff(got, want string) string {
65: 	g := strings.Split(got, "\n")
66: 	w := strings.Split(want, "\n")
67: 	for i := 0; ; i++ {
68: 		switch {
69: 		case i < len(g) && i < len(w):
70: 			if g[i] == w[i] {
71: 				continue
72: 			}
73: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- first difference in line %d:\n"+
74: 				"-- got : %q\n-- want: %q\n", i+1, g[i], w[i])
75: 		case i < len(g):
76: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d extra lines after line %d:\n"+
77: 				"-- first extra line: %q\n", len(g)-len(w), i, g[i])
78: 		case i < len(w):
79: 			return fmt.Sprintf("-- got %d correct lines, want %d more lines:\n"+
80: 				"-- want next: %q\n", i, len(w)-i, w[i])
81: 		default:
82: 			return "no differences found"
83: 		}
84: 	}
85: }

## Summary

Implemented the song algorithmically in `food_chain.go` (no new files, test file untouched):

- **`animals`** — the 8 animals in order (fly → horse).
- **`comments`** — map of verse number → the animal-specific comment line (e.g. "What a hog, to swallow a dog!"; the fly has none, the horse gets "She's dead, of course!").
- **`catchers`** — map of animal index → modifier used when the animal appears as prey; only the spider carries one ("that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her"), so the `bird` verse correctly reads "…to catch the spider that wriggled and jiggled and tickled inside her." while the `spider` verse reads "…to catch the fly."
- **`Verse(v)`** — builds the opening line, the comment (if any), then the cumulative "She swallowed the X to catch the Y" chain walking backwards through the food chain, and ends with "Perhaps she'll die" — except the horse verse, which has no catch lines and no "perhaps she'll die" line.
- **`Verses(start, end)`** / **`Song()`** — join the requested verse range with blank lines; `Song()` is `Verses(1, 8)`.

Test results: `TestVerse` (all 8 verses), `TestVerses`, and `TestSong` all pass.
